public_rationale: Under the ordinary reading that the released GPT-5 itself would not achieve broadly general human-level intelligence, the forecast is supported. The release assessment and METR’s documented capability gaps jointly satisfy the early-resolution rule. GPT-5’s strong software-engineering performance is material context, but strength in that domain does not establish general human-level capability. This conclusion depends on the stated interpretation of AGI and GPT-5; it does not establish a claim about every future derivative.
limitations: Marcus supplied neither an AGI definition nor a numerical threshold.
The explicit launch assessment is reported by a reputable newspaper; a directly readable primary transcript was not obtained.
METR evaluated GPT-5 Thinking, not every GPT-5 configuration, and its study focused on autonomous technical tasks.
METR disclosed that OpenAI reviewed and approved publication under its access agreement.
METR identified defective or disadvantaged tasks as well as genuine failures. Only its validated failures are used here.

statement.excerpt: GPT-5 will not bring us to AGI.
statement.document_title: How China might crush the West in the race to AGI if we don’t up our regulatory game

from_speaker: will not bring us to AGI
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that GPT-5 itself would not achieve broadly general human-level intelligence, including the ability to handle unfamiliar tasks reliably.
I interpret GPT-5 as the released system bearing that name, including its reasoning capabilities. This does not extend the claim to every successor or future system built using GPT-5.
Marcus supplied no numerical test or definition of AGI. Strong performance in individual domains does not alone settle whether intelligence is broadly general.
The forecast has no calendar deadline. Release and substantive capability evaluations can nevertheless settle this model-specific prediction.

criteria.contradiction_condition: The released GPT-5 demonstrates broadly general human-level intelligence through credible, independently corroborated evaluations across unfamiliar tasks and domains.
